Hi Alice — looping in answers to the technical bullets below. Short version up front: we support BYOK via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can integrate with customer HSMs for Private deployments. We do not store plaintext customer keys. Details: 

- Key ownership and BYOK: Customers provision keys in their own KMS account. Redwood is granted usage/crypto permissions via KMS key policies (Encrypt/Decrypt) but never receives the plaintext key material. For Dedicated/Private we can also configure an HSM-backed keystore where the key material is never exportable. 

- Rotation: Key rotation is controlled by the customer KMS policy. When rotation occurs, Redwood services reference the latest key version via the KMS API. We recommend a 30- to 90-day rotation cadence for sensitive workloads; we can support ad-hoc rotations with zero-downtime rewrap procedures. 

- Audit & logging: All key operations (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) are logged in the customer KMS and can be forwarded to their Cloud Audit logs / SIEM. For Dedicated/Private we can stream usage logs to a customer-managed destination. Redwood also logs logical access events (who requested operations) and correlates them for incident response; those logs can be included in SOC 2 artifact packages. 

- In-transit/at-rest: TLS 1.2+ for transit, AES-256 for at-rest encryption of persisted artifacts. KV cache (in-memory) uses ephemeral encryption keys derived per-process and is never written to disk in plaintext.

- HSM options: For customers requiring FIPS 140-2 / Level 3 HSMs, we partner with HSM providers and can deploy a hardware-backed keystore for Private deployments; that model supports customer key ownership and non-exportability.

If helpful, Michael is available for a 45-min deep technical session to walk through the KMS flow, key policies, and a demo of rotation and logs. Suggested time windows next Tue/Wed morning PST.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
